design_detail: Update, by one author, of his own 2011 review of epidemiological evidence on snus and health, limited to cancers, circulatory disease and oral conditions. Searches were 'updated to 18 November 2012' and nine new publications were found; databases, search terms and selection criteria are not given in this paper (methods are 'as previously described' in the 2011 review, which was not read). Results are summarised narratively, with one small meta-analysis (fixed and random effects) of 13 published relative risks or odds ratios for heart attack or ischaemic heart disease in never-smoking Swedish men, and a second of fatal and non-fatal heart attack in five studies. The update was supported by a snus manufacturer and the author is a long-term consultant to the tobacco industry.
can_establish: How this author, with these funders, read the epidemiological evidence on snus and cancer, heart attack, heart failure and oral disease as of November 2012, and what his pooling of published heart-attack estimates in never-smoking Swedish men gives under his choices of studies and exclusions.
cannot_establish: Whether snus is harmful or harmless: the search and selection are not described in this paper, the cited studies are not appraised against a standard, null and positive findings are not scrutinised alike, the pooling mixes designs and adjustment sets and drops one estimate after the fact, the evidence stops in 2012 (before the 2020 pooled mortality analysis and the 2023 cancer review), and the comparison with smoking is asserted more than shown.

sample.recruitment: Search of unnamed sources 'updated to 18th November 2012' following the 2011 review; no databases, terms or flow of records are given. 'Results are only summarized for health effects where new relevant publications could be identified' (Methods, Results). The update was prompted by two recent publications the author regarded as major new findings, one on pancreatic cancer and one on heart attack (Background, 3rd paragraph).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Not stated in this paper. For the heart-attack pooling: male never smokers only, and earlier results from the same cohorts that were superseded by later reports were left out of Table 1. One estimate (the Construction Workers Study interviews of 1971 to 1974) was later left out of a second pooling because of differences in the type of snus, limited and ambiguously coded questionnaire data, and its being based only on fatal cases (Results › Circulatory disease, 2nd paragraph).
sample.demographics: Swedish men, almost entirely. The Construction Workers Study contributed 88% of the person-years in the pooled heart-attack analysis (Results › Circulatory disease, 4th paragraph). Other samples are local population surveys, hospital-based case-control studies and registers.
sample.selection_effects: Evidence is selected by the author; the update is built on his own earlier reviews and was triggered by two papers he judged important. The citations are mainly Swedish cohort and case-control studies, and the direct evidence on several outcomes (for example the oesophagus and stomach) is carried from the 2011 review and not shown here.

exposure.measurement: Current or ever use of snus as recorded in each cited study (questionnaire or interview at baseline in cohorts; interview in case-control studies). Exposure is mostly a single recording and the review does not discuss that limitation for the null findings.
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Not synthesised. The text states that nicotine exposure from snus is similar to, and perhaps somewhat greater than, that from smoking (Background, 1st paragraph, citing earlier physiological studies). Route: oral.
exposure.polysubstance: Handled by analysing male never smokers and, separately, all men with adjustment for smoking; the pancreatic and heart-disease conclusions differ between these in some studies.

comparison.controls: People who never used snus (and, in the never-smoker analyses, never smoked), in each cited study.
comparison.matching: Adjustment varies by study from none or age only to six factors (Table 1, adjustment column).
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not discussed systematically. The author raises confounding by socio-economic status, alcohol, area of residence and health care for the positive findings, much less for the null ones.
comparison.controls_other_drug_use: Alcohol is raised as a possible confounder for one Norwegian study only (Results › Pancreatic cancer, 2nd paragraph).

outcomes.instruments: Published estimates of cancers (pancreas, oral cavity and oropharynx, colon, rectum, anus, acoustic neuroma), survival after cancer, heart attack and ischaemic heart disease (fatal and non-fatal), heart failure, periodontitis and caries.
outcomes.validity_norms: Not assessed. Outcomes are taken as the cited studies defined them.
outcomes.operationalization: Harm is a significantly raised risk estimate in the cited studies; 'unassociated' is used where estimates were not significant, without intervals being weighed against the size of a risk that would matter.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Not applicable (single author, no duplicate selection or extraction described).

analysis.effect_sizes: Pancreatic cancer (earlier review of nine North American and two Scandinavian studies on smokeless tobacco): smoking-adjusted RR 1.07 (0.71 to 1.60) in seven studies and 1.23 (0.67 to 2.31) in never smokers in five; the Scandinavian cohort of construction workers 2.00 (1.20 to 3.30) in never smokers and 0.90 (0.70 to 1.20) smoking-adjusted; the Norwegian cohort 0.85 (0.24 to 3.07) in never smokers and 1.67 (1.12 to 1.50 as printed) smoking-adjusted; the two combined 1.61 (0.77 to 3.34) in never smokers and 1.20 (0.66 to 2.20) smoking-adjusted. New: pooled analysis of 11 case-control studies of smokeless tobacco other than snus, none in Scandinavia, OR 0.98 (0.75 to 1.27) for ever use and 0.62 (0.37 to 1.04) for smokeless tobacco only. Oropharyngeal cancer (2011 review): RR 1.01 (0.71 to 1.45, 4 estimates) in never smokers, 0.97 (0.68 to 1.37, 7 estimates) smoking-adjusted. Colon (153 exposed cases) and rectal (97) cancer in 336,381 construction workers: no association shown, intervals not given in the text; anal cancer 1 case. Acoustic neuroma (451 cases, 710 controls): current snus OR 0.94 (0.57 to 1.55), former 1.22 (0.71 to 2.10), current smoking 0.41 (0.23 to 0.74). Survival after any cancer in 40,320 [sic] male construction workers: all-cause RR 1.13 (1.05 to 1.20) for snus only, 1.21 (1.17 to 1.25) for smoking only, 1.17 (1.12 to 1.22) for both; cancer-specific RR 1.15 (1.05 to 1.26) for snus only, 1.15 (1.10 to 1.21) for smoking only. Heart attack or ischaemic heart disease in never-smoking Swedish men, 13 estimates: fixed-effect RR 1.07 (0.98 to 1.16), heterogeneity p = 0.06; random-effects 1.06 (0.91 to 1.23); without the 1971 to 1974 construction-worker estimate (1.35, 1.13 to 1.62, fatal cases only) 12 estimates: fixed 1.00 (0.91 to 1.10), random 1.00 (0.88 to 1.13). Pooled analysis of eight cohorts (cited): incidence RR 1.04 (0.93 to 1.17), short-term fatality OR 1.28 (0.99 to 1.68). Five studies: fatal cases RR 1.31 (1.09 to 1.58), non-fatal 0.89 (0.79 to 1.00), ratio 1.48 (1.19 to 1.84). Heart failure: construction workers RR 1.28 (1.00 to 1.64, 75 cases); Uppsala cohort 2.08 (1.03 to 4.22, 14 cases). Periodontitis and caries: no raised risk after adjustment for age, sex and sociodemographic variables in random population samples.
analysis.covariates: Per cited study (Table 1 lists: age; age and residence; age, exercise, health, illness, residence, socio-economic status; age, BMI, cholesterol, education, leisure and physical activity; none). Many cited estimates are adjusted for age only.
analysis.selective_reporting: Results are given only for conditions with a new publication since 2011. The heart-attack pooling drops the only significantly raised estimate in a second pooling on grounds given after the data were in; the 13-estimate result is also shown. Confidence intervals are missing for the colorectal and some other findings.
analysis.power: Not discussed for the null findings: several heart-attack estimates rest on fewer than 10 exposed cases (for example 0, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8 cases among the eight pooled cohorts), and cancers such as anal cancer on one case.

interpretation_gap.results_show: The paper summarises nine publications since 2011. For pancreatic cancer it reports no new snus study, only a pooled analysis of other smokeless tobacco products, with an earlier two-cohort summary showing a wide interval. For heart attack, the 13-estimate pooling gives 1.07 (0.98 to 1.16), 1.00 when one estimate is dropped, while fatal heart attacks were raised (1.31, 1.09 to 1.58) and non-fatal ones slightly lower (0.89) in five studies. Death after a cancer diagnosis was raised in men who used snus only (1.13 all causes, 1.15 cancer-specific) about as much as in men who smoked only (1.21 and 1.15). Heart failure was higher in two small analyses.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract says the new evidence 'further undermines' the argument that snus raises pancreatic cancer risk, extends the list of cancers unassociated with snus (oropharynx, oesophagus, stomach, lung, now colorectal and acoustic neuroma), and says that even if some adverse effects exist they are far less than those of smoking; the conclusions say any cancer risk is at most minimal. Gaps: (1) there is no new snus study on pancreatic cancer, and the pooled analysis said to undermine the argument concerns other forms of smokeless tobacco, with no Scandinavian study; (2) 'unassociated' is read from non-significant estimates, several from few cases and one-time exposure measures, and no interval is given for colorectal findings; (3) no oesophagus, stomach or lung data are shown in this update, so their listing rests on the 2011 review; (4) 'far less than smoking' is not shown here for cancer survival, where cause-specific mortality ratios are the same for snus only and smoking only (1.15 and 1.15); (5) the sentence in the Discussion that effects if any are probably no more than 1% of those of smoking is carried over from the 2011 review without derivation; (6) positive findings are met with critique of method (confounding, exposure group, follow-up), null findings with much less; (7) the stated preference to treat the 1971 to 1974 construction-worker estimate as an outlier is argued after the fact.

timeline.event: European Commission scientific committee report on smokeless tobacco cited the pancreas as a target organ; the author calls its reading misleading because it reported only the significant associations.

The author's comprehensive review and meta-analysis of snus and health, which this paper updates; its 'scant support for any major adverse health effects' conclusion is restated in the Background (not read).
Pooled analysis of eight Swedish cohorts on heart attack (Hansson et al.): no raised incidence, higher short-term fatality (OR 1.28, 0.99 to 1.68), as cited here.
Pooled analysis of eight Swedish cohorts on mortality: higher all-cause (HR 1.28), cardiovascular (1.27) and cancer (1.12) death in men using snus only against men who never used tobacco.
Systematic review of cancer risk among men using snus only, with industry-linked and industry-sponsored studies excluded by design; found graded evidence of higher risk for some cancers.

replication.where_it_stands: A decade-old, single-author update that supplies the industry-supported reading of the 2000s and early 2010s evidence. Its main specific findings (no overall heart-attack incidence signal in never-smoking men; fatal heart attack and post-cancer mortality raised) have been reproduced in direction by later pooled analyses (byhamre_2021), and its reading of pancreatic and oesophageal cancer is disputed by the 2023 independent review (valen_2023). Newer data now exist that this paper could not include.

funding.funder: Supported by Swedish Match (a snus manufacturer); some of the earlier reviews underpinning it were supported by Philip Morris Products and the European Smokeless Tobacco Council (Acknowledgements). The paper states the sponsor had no involvement in the planning, execution or writing of the manuscript or the decision to submit it.
funding.declared_conflicts: The author is a long-term consultant to the tobacco industry; he describes the paper as an independent scientific assessment, the views being his alone (Competing interests).
funding.affiliations_note: Single author, who also wrote, alone or with co-authors, several of the earlier reviews on which the conclusions rest (the 2011 review on snus, and earlier reviews on smokeless tobacco and circulatory disease, oral disease, pancreatic cancer and cancer in general). Industry support is declared for this update and for some of those reviews; the text read does not say which. Recorded as a flag for closer reading, not as a reason to discount the findings; every finding of this review is set beside independent work on the same question in the claim.

what_would_settle_it: A systematic review with a registered protocol, named databases, explicit criteria, duplicate selection and extraction and a standard bias assessment of every cohort, applying the same scrutiny to null and positive estimates, by authors and funders without tobacco-industry ties (or with an independent second team repeating the extraction); and individual-participant pooling of the Swedish and Norwegian cohorts with tobacco use updated through follow-up, which exists in part in the 2020 and 2023 papers.

domains.note: A search date is given but no databases, terms, criteria or selection process; the methods are by reference to the 2011 review.

Some studies are criticised in text (confounding by alcohol, mixed exposure group, long follow-up without updating, interview-year coding in the construction-worker data) but there is no standard bias assessment of any cited study.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: The conclusions rest on the author's own earlier reviews and meta-analyses (the 2011 review and four earlier reviews on specific diseases), some supported by tobacco companies and an industry council.
Mostly separated, but 'far less than smoking', 'at most minimal' and the 1% of smoking figure are asserted rather than shown here, and policy opinions about switching are included in the Discussion.

domains.domain: Balance of evidence for and against harm
domains.note: Findings of harm are examined closely for method flaws; null findings from small, single-baseline-measure cohorts are taken at face value; the pooling that removes the one significantly raised estimate is justified after the fact. The side under-represented is the evidence of harm.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No standard risk-of-bias instrument applies to a narrative review (METHODS §5.3). The paper is explicit about its funders and declares the author's industry ties, and it prints the underlying numbers for its pooling, which can be rechecked; but selection is unsystematic, the cited studies are not appraised alike, and the author relies on his own earlier work. It may be cited as the industry-supported author's reading of the evidence to 2012, for the numbers it reports from primary studies (to be checked against those studies), and for the heart-attack pooling as an unweighted-by-quality summary; not as evidence that snus is harmless, and never alone.

key_findings.finding: Funding and interests as printed: the update was supported by Swedish Match, with some earlier reviews supported by Philip Morris Products and the European Smokeless Tobacco Council; the sponsor is stated to have had no involvement; the author is a long-term consultant to the tobacco industry and calls the work an independent scientific assessment.
Search updated to 18 November 2012 after the 2011 review; nine new relevant publications identified; methods otherwise 'as previously described'.

Pancreatic cancer: no new study of snus. A pooled analysis of 11 case-control studies of other smokeless tobacco, none in Scandinavia, gave OR 0.98 (0.75 to 1.27) for ever use and 0.62 (0.37 to 1.04) for smokeless tobacco only, against never use of tobacco; earlier combined Scandinavian cohorts gave 1.61 (0.77 to 3.34) in never smokers and 1.20 (0.66 to 2.20) smoking-adjusted. The author concludes the evidence for a link was weak and is weaker.

Colorectal cancer in 336,381 male construction workers followed to 2007: no association of snus-only use with colon (153 exposed cases) or rectal (97) cancer, age- and BMI-adjusted; intervals not printed; anal cancer, 1 exposed case. Acoustic neuroma: current snus OR 0.94 (0.57 to 1.55), current smoking 0.41 (0.23 to 0.74).

Oral cancer: 16 men with oral squamous cell carcinoma at the exact site of snus use in seven hospitals (a case series); the author notes there is no comparison information on site distribution; earlier pooled oropharyngeal estimates were close to 1 (1.01 and 0.97); a follow-up of 1,115 people with the snus-related oral lesion found no cancers at the lesion sites.

Survival after a cancer diagnosis in construction workers: all-cause RR 1.13 (1.05 to 1.20) for snus only, 1.21 (1.17 to 1.25) for smoking only, 1.17 (1.12 to 1.22) for both, against never tobacco; cancer-specific RR 1.15 (1.05 to 1.26) for snus only and 1.15 (1.10 to 1.21) for smoking only; stage at diagnosis not controlled.

Heart attack or ischaemic heart disease in never-smoking Swedish men: 13 estimates pooled, fixed-effect RR 1.07 (0.98 to 1.16), heterogeneity p = 0.06, random-effects 1.06 (0.91 to 1.23); leaving out the construction-worker interview estimate of 1971 to 1974 (1.35, 1.13 to 1.62, fatal cases only) gives 12 estimates, fixed 1.00 (0.91 to 1.10), random 1.00 (0.88 to 1.13). Several of the 13 estimates are adjusted for age only.

Case fatality: in five studies, fatal heart attack RR 1.31 (1.09 to 1.58) and non-fatal 0.89 (0.79 to 1.00), ratio 1.48 (1.19 to 1.84); in the pooled eight-cohort analysis incidence RR 1.04 (0.93 to 1.17) and short-term fatality OR 1.28 (0.99 to 1.68), with the Construction Workers Study 88% of person-years. The author asks whether the fatality excess is a direct effect or confounding.
key_findings.locator: Results › Circulatory disease, 3rd and 4th paragraphs; Table 2

key_findings.finding: Heart failure: Construction Workers Study RR 1.28 (1.00 to 1.64) in never smokers with 75 exposed cases, no dose-response by daily amount; Uppsala cohort RR 2.08 (1.03 to 4.22) with 14 exposed cases, smokers and non-smokers combined.
Periodontitis and dental caries: random population samples of one Swedish city at three time points showed no raised risk after adjustment for age, sex and sociodemographic variables.
key_findings.locator: Results › Periodontitis and dental caries, 2nd paragraph

key_findings.finding: The author's conclusions: adverse health effects of snus have not been clearly identified; any cancer risk is at most minimal and much less than for smoking; snus might adversely affect survival from cancer; reports of increased fatal heart attack and heart failure need investigation. He restates that any effects on cancer or circulatory disease, if they exist, are probably no more than 1% of those of smoking (a figure from the 2011 review) and that switching should improve the health prospects of smokers who cannot give up nicotine.

reporting_issues.issue: The Norwegian cohort's smoking-adjusted pancreatic cancer estimate is printed as 1.67 (95% CI 1.12 to 1.50): the upper limit is below the point estimate.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Results › Pancreatic cancer, 1st paragraph
reporting_issues.consequence: A misprint. IARC Monograph 100E (sc_iarc_2012) prints the same estimate as 1.67 (1.12 to 2.50; 45 cases), so the upper limit is very probably 2.50; this was not checked against the primary paper.

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract says the additional evidence 'further undermines' the pancreatic cancer argument, but the text states there are no new studies of pancreatic cancer and snus; the new pooled analysis concerns smokeless tobacco other than snus, with no Scandinavian study.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Abstract; Results › Pancreatic cancer, 2nd paragraph
reporting_issues.consequence: The new evidence is indirect for snus; a claim must not present it as a new snus finding.

reporting_issues.issue: The Construction Workers Study's non-fatal heart-attack estimate is given as RR 0.70 (0.48 to 1.02) in the text and as 0.94 (0.83 to 1.06) in Table 2 for the same earlier report.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Results › Circulatory disease, 4th paragraph; Table 2 (Hergens et al. row)
reporting_issues.consequence: The non-fatal estimate for the main cohort is uncertain by about a quarter; the primary paper must be checked before it is quoted.

reporting_issues.issue: Heterogeneity of p = 0.06 is called significant, although significance is defined as p < 0.05 elsewhere in the same section.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Results › Circulatory disease, 1st and 2nd paragraphs
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; the choice to drop one estimate rests on this heterogeneity and on three explanations given for that estimate.

reporting_issues.issue: The text gives 40,320 male construction workers in the cancer-survival study, whereas the cited paper's title (in the reference list) gives 40,230.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Results › Survival from cancer, 1st paragraph; reference list
reporting_issues.consequence: A transposition; the cited paper's number is 40,230 (also used in the 2023 review).

reporting_issues.issue: The rendered reference list is unnumbered and at least one citation (the 'strong' cohort studies cited for pancreatic cancer) does not match the reference in the matching position.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Results › Pancreatic cancer, 2nd paragraph; reference list
reporting_issues.consequence: Numbered citations in this paper cannot all be traced to a reference with certainty; findings here are attributed by the study names the text gives.

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC4029226 (all sections, Tables 1 and 2 rendered as text, competing interests and acknowledgements read; the reference list was read but is rendered without numbers; the 2011 review that supplies the methods was not read)
